positions.title: Computer Engineer
positions.locationName: Washington, District of Columbia, United States · On-site
positions.description:
• Designed hardware APIs to standardize communication protocols across 8 camera sensors, 2 inertial navigation systems, and 1 temperature control unity, ensuring seamless integration regardless of manufacturer SDKs or hardware protocols.  
• Created signal processing IP modules utilizing the Xilinx FPGA family and VHDL to monitor signals across multiple domains. 
• Implemented a robust camera calibration pipeline in Python to correct commonly encountered anomalies in optical sensors within the spectrum. Pipeline used to verify contractor measurements for approximately 100+ hours of imagery data. 
• Developed a full-stack software application for flight tests, saving the Navy approximately $50,000 in contract costs. The backend was built in C++, with a component-based frontend implemented in Lua.
positions.insights: Skills: Computer Science · Electrical Engineering · Embedded Devices · Embedded Software

positions.title: Electrical Engineer
positions.description:
Civilian
• Authored a test plan, 2 reports, and a data package for the $2 Billion Skyborg Autonomous Attritable Aircraft Experiment (AAAx) that led to an early transition to a United States Air Force (USAF) Program of Record 6 months ahead of schedule
• Led and coordinated a team of 9 engineers, 2 contractors (General Atomics and Lockheed Martin), and the Air Force Research Laboratory during the Orange Flag Multi-Domain test event to demonstrate the integration of different sensor payloads with a modular autonomy architecture
• Developed 3 performance measures (lethality, survivability, and situation awareness) that evaluate the competitive
advantage of Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) to guide the development and acquisition of autonomous systems/concepts
• Evaluated the Legion Pod’s (an Infrared Search and Track Sensor) ability to support future manned-unmanned teaming experimentation by utilizing Python to analyze approximately 50 hours of sensor data
• Created a Plotly dashboard in Databricks to help Air Force leadership identify and improve areas of necessity for future hiring decisions as part of the first ever data hackathon across the Air Force Test Centers (AFTC)

positions.title: Research And Development Intern
positions.description:
• Utilized MATLAB to perform signal processing techniques with least-squares algorithm and FFT filters in order to extrapolate amplitude and phase data from voltage signal readings using an FPGA.
• Created plots for data analysis to determine the accuracy of MATLAB toolsets.
• Contributed to IEEE paper “Techniques for Digital Array Radar Planar Near-Field Calibration by Retrofit of an Analog System” in order to develop proper calibration techniques for digital antenna arrays in a near field range.

positions.title: Test Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Developed a test plan and report for a radar warning receiver system utilizing 4 separate maneuvers and 13 emitters
• Programmed with MATLAB and Python to perform data analysis on flight test data utilizing the DIVA RF analysis software
• Received a certificate of completion for the Integrated Air Defense Systems Software (IADS) from 40 hours of training to utilize mission control software
• Completed a course in the foundational aspects of a radar warning receiver with a collective 40 hours of training

positions.title: Peer Instructor
positions.description:
• Largest student run makerspace in the nation with 2500+ average attendees each month open to all majors and members of the Georgia Tech community.	
• Maintained facility equipment, assisted new users to the space, and trained new members
• Taught members of the community to use 3D printers, $20,000+ plasma cutters, multiple channel oscilloscopes, and signal generators.

positions.title: Research Development Engineering Intern
positions.description:
• Developed tests to characterize the resolution of a radio transceiver in a collaborative project with the Department of Navy and the University of Maryland
• Utilized a $10,000 motion capture system to collect positioning data on autonomous UAVs
• Programmed with MAVROS and Python to further the development in new Naval SWARM robotics laboratory
• Designed a monopulse, continuous wave, and pulsed radar using a software defined radio within the GNU radio program.

honors.title: SMART Scholar
honors.description:
• Competitive Department of Defense Scholarship
• Service Commitment

volunteerExperiences.description:
• Developed and coordinated STEM program for the Boys and Girls Club of Southern Maryland that involved coodination with the program director and other volunteers.
• Created a computer lab for members of the club consisting of 8 computers with RAM and SSD upgrades to save the club approximately $1000 in parts.

projects.title: Automatic Concussion Evaluation (ACE) | Senior Capstone
projects.description:
• Partnered with NSIN in order to develop and test 5 embedded boards with electrodes within a military helmet to detect possible concussions using an EEG device.
•Utilized C programming language to create hardware libraries for the STM32 processor in order to perform operations with peripheral chipsets including the ADXL372 accelerometer and MX25R6435F flash memory unit.
•Utilized the CMSIS digital signal processing library in order to develop a bandpass filter from 1-55 Hz in order to isolate desired frequency spectrum for a concussion event.
